data_requests.item: Existing tower-water service, treatment target, conductivity and makeup/blowdown balance records
where: site records: Existing named tower/system service and water-treatment logs, chemistry limits/target basis, conductivity and makeup/blowdown flow or volume records, installed control/meter function and loss/component records. Retain source/revision, actual subject association, units, calibration/availability, sample times and matching operating intervals.

a walkdown: Only if existing records leave an applicable question unresolved: agree safe observations with the responsible water-treatment/engineering specialist. No compulsory new meter, measurement, chemical treatment or operating change.
data_requests.how: Establish evaporative recirculating-water applicability first; known dry-only air-cooled service is not applicable and unknown service remains conditional. A nearby generic analyzer or meter label does not prove the water function, suitability or absence of other meters. For comparable quantities/units and matched periods, review conductivity/concentration ratio together with the makeup-to-blowdown flow/volume ratio, the treatment specialist's chemistry-limited target and operating coverage. Preserve conversions and uncertainty; raw incompatible quantities or periods cannot be divided as if comparable. Disagreement calls for records/component/loss review including leaks, overflow, drift or other draw-off, not an automatic higher target. Complete suitable existing records or a justified chemistry limit may be acknowledged without a new measurement/retrofit; source examplecycles are not site targets.

questions.decision_rule: Review existing chemistry/treatment limits, matched water balance and conductivity evidence, installed functions and unresolved losses with the responsible specialist before any change. Do not raise cycles, install a controller/meter or alter treatment from a manual/no-analyzer pattern or a source example alone. Existing suitable control and chemistry-limited operation may be acknowledged. Unknown source, association, units or time coverage remains explicit; this screen is not a hardware decision or site saving.

typical_benefit.wording: "Increasing cycles from three to six reduces cooling tower make-up water by 20% and cooling tower blowdown by 50%." Recommends a conductivity controller and makeup/blowdown flow meters. No energy % stated.

questions.limits: IAC/ITAC figures are browse-page averages read through a summarizing fetch and not re-verified against the downloadable database; averages are skewed by outliers. Source-informed records review: S21 applies to evaporative tower-water management and requires chemistry-constrained targets, matched conductivity/flow logs and loss/component checks. Named instruments and filled fields are unverified candidates, not completion or source authority; inherited example benefits are not site savings.
